title: Kestrel Dispensing Standard: Emergency Supply on Prescriptions
content:
An emergency supply is a pharmacist's dispensing of a maintenance medication under Kestrel Prescriptions when no refill is available.

## Clauses

1. **When it may be dispensed.** An emergency supply is dispensed only for a prescription in active or expired status whose class allows an emergency supply, when the prescription has no refill available or has expired, and when a renewal request sent to the prescriber has had no reply for at least the class's resend business days.
2. **Size.** Its days supply is the smaller of the class's largest emergency supply days and the prescription's written days supply.
3. **Frequency.** The number of emergency supplies on the prescription in the rolling 365 days — the 365 calendar days ending today, today included — must be below the class's limit per 365 days.
4. **Effect.** It consumes no refill and does not reactivate an expired prescription.
5. **Classes excluded.** Controlled and specialty classes never receive an emergency supply at Kestrel; the patient is referred to the prescriber.

The status, the remaining refills, the renewal request and its reply are all read from the system records.

## Days supply worked through (hypothetical class maximum of 14 days)

| Prescription's written days supply | Emergency supply days |
|---|---|
| 30 | 14 (the smaller of 14 and 30) |
| 10 | 10 (the smaller of 14 and 10) |

## Conditions together (hypothetical records)

| Status | Refill available | Renewal request unanswered for the class's resend business days | Emergency supply |
|---|---|---|---|
| active | no | yes | may be dispensed, within the yearly limit |
| expired | any | yes | may be dispensed, within the yearly limit |
| active | yes | any | not dispensed |
| active | no | no request sent | not dispensed |
| discontinued | any | any | not dispensed |

**Does the emergency supply restart an expired prescription?** No; it does not reactivate an expired prescription.
